01.r: Jesus asks them to produce the coin.
01.n: An aorist imperative, a single act: show it now. Abbott-Smith lists this verse under 'to show, exhibit'.

03.r: The Roman coin Jesus asks to see.
03.n: Abbott-Smith calls it 'the Lat. denarius, a Roman coin, nearly equal to the δραχμή'. The KJV's 'penny' puts an English coin in its place; this study keeps the coin's own name.

04.r: Asks to whom the image belongs.

05.r: What the coin bears on its face.

06.r: The portrait struck on the coin.
06.n: Abbott-Smith gives 'an image, likeness' and lists this verse. He notes that in the Septuagint it chiefly renders Hebrew צֶלֶם.

08.r: The lettering on the coin, naming its ruler.
08.n: Abbott-Smith gives 'an inscription'. The KJV's 'superscription' is its old word for writing placed on something.

09.r: The article used as a pronoun with δέ: the questioners.

11.n: The KJV, Geneva, DRC and YLT all add 'answered' or 'answering'; nothing in our Greek text answers to it.

12.r: The coin bears the emperor's image and name.

tr_note: The Textus Receptus reads ἐπιδείξατε, a compound of the same verb, for δείξατε; both mean 'show', and the KJV's 'Shew' is the same either way. It also lacks the article οἱ that our text uses for 'they'; the KJV's 'They answered and said' has an 'answered' for which our text has no word.
